item.title: CView: Crystal Structure Visualization & Analysis
item.description:
What it does

CView is a desktop crystal-structure viewer, written in Rust with GTK 4. It sits between looking at a structure and setting up a calculation on it: you open a file, check and modify the structure, and write the input for the next calculation. It is built for disordered materials — alongside ordered structures it handles the site occupations that describe a random alloy, and exports them to SPR-KKR for coherent-potential calculations.

  • Read and write the common formats: VASP, Quantum ESPRESSO (including the final structure of a vc-relax run), SPR-KKR, CIF, XYZ and extended XYZ, PDB, and LAMMPS trajectories.
  • Symmetry: space-group detection, and conversion between primitive and conventional cells.
  • Build structures: supercells, surface slabs for any Miller plane, and searches for voids and intercalation sites.
  • Reciprocal space: the first Brillouin zone and its standard high-symmetry k-path, drawn in 3D.
  • Simulated X-ray diffraction, to compare a model structure with a measured pattern.
  • Figures: export the view as PDF or transparent PNG for papers.

The main view draws on the CPU, so it runs on an ordinary laptop. Only the charge-density isosurface and trajectory player windows use OpenGL.

The method and its validation are described in the paper in the Journal of Applied Crystallography.

Quick Start

CView runs on Linux, Windows and macOS. Ready-to-install packages are on the Releases page. To build from source, you need Rust and the GTK 4 development files (on Fedora: sudo dnf install gtk4-devel):

git clone https://github.com/mavensgroup/cview.git
cd cview
cargo run --release

The documentation covers installation on every platform and each tool in detail.

item.title: MkBib: Bibliography Manager
item.description:
What it does

MkBib is a desktop manager for BibTeX bibliographies, written in Rust with GTK 4 and libadwaita. It is built for the .bib files that grow over years of writing papers and theses.

  • Large libraries: opens databases of more than 10,000 entries without delay.
  • Search: filter entries by author, year or title as you type.
  • Edit: double-click an entry to change its fields.
  • Validation: checks entries against the fields BibLaTeX requires, so a missing field shows up in MkBib rather than as a LaTeX compilation error.
  • Safe saving: writes the file atomically, so an interrupted save cannot corrupt your library.

Quick Start

MkBib needs Rust and the GTK 4 and libadwaita development files (on Fedora: sudo dnf install gtk4-devel libadwaita-devel gcc).

git clone https://github.com/mavens-group/mkbib.git
cd mkbib
cargo install --path . --root ~/.local
mkbib-rs library.bib

The README gives the packages for Debian, Ubuntu and Arch Linux.

item.title: Ptbl: Periodic Table
item.description:
What it does

Ptbl is a periodic table for the Linux desktop, built with GTK 4 and libadwaita. It works offline.

  • Browse all 118 elements, coloured by category, with up to 40 properties per element on six tabs.
  • Search and filter: find an element by symbol or name as you type, or highlight one category, such as the transition metals.
  • Colour by property: turn the table into a heatmap of one of eight properties.
  • Trend charts: plot atomic, covalent or van der Waals radius, or electron affinity, against atomic number.
  • Vegard’s law calculator: estimate the lattice parameters, cell volume and density of an alloy from its composition, then open the structure in CView or export it as a CIF file.

Atomic and thermal properties come from a bundled snapshot of the PubChem periodic table. Some crystal, electrical, magnetic and nuclear values come from earlier versions of Ptbl and haven’t yet been checked against current sources, so verify them before relying on them. Vegard’s-law results are quick estimates, not a substitute for a calculation or a measurement.

Quick Start

Ptbl needs Linux, Python 3.10 or newer, and GTK 4.12, libadwaita 1.5 and PyGObject from your distribution’s packages (on Fedora: sudo dnf install gtk4 libadwaita python3-gobject).

python3 -m pip install --user git+https://github.com/mavens-group/Ptbl.git
ptbl

On Debian, Ubuntu and Arch Linux, add --break-system-packages. The README covers every distribution, virtual environments and troubleshooting.
